composite: The composite salience index printed 55.9 on 2026-08-07, held up by Gulf and energy coverage at 76.3 and Pakistan at 68.0 while shipping attention fell 23.9 points below its seven-day average and US trade rose 21.3 points above its own.

channels.pakistan_west: Pakistan and Western Border scored 68.0, down 18.9 points from the 86.9 seven-day average, on 56 articles with only 5.4 percent from tier-one and tier-two outlets. Coverage clustered on Indus water sharing claims, Pakistan's acquisition of Chinese howitzers, and the PoK vote and related protests, none of it carried by the largest outlets.
channels.china_east: China and Eastern Border scored 27.3, up 1.1 points from the 26.2 seven-day average, the quietest channel on the board. Only 14 articles were logged, at 14.3 percent tier-one and tier-two share, spread across stalled India-China border trade over a tax row, high-altitude drone logistics, and reporting on Beijing's handling of Tibetan sacred sites.
channels.gulf_energy: Gulf and Energy Security scored 76.3, off 0.7 points from the 76.9 seven-day average and still the highest channel reading. Volume hit the 150-article ceiling with an 84 percent tier-one and tier-two share, driven by reports that an Iran-US Strait of Hormuz arrangement is close, Iranian mixed signals on talks, and Israeli casualties in Lebanon.
channels.us_trade: US and Trade Policy scored 46.1, up 21.3 points from the 24.8 seven-day average, the largest gain of the day. The 83 articles at 18.1 percent tier-one and tier-two share leaned on US visa and green card rule changes, a sharp drop in F-1 visas issued to Indian and Chinese students, and domestic argument over opening digital payments to US firms.
channels.shipping: Shipping and Chokepoints scored 61.7, down 23.9 points from the 85.6 seven-day average despite hitting the 150-article ceiling, with tier-one and tier-two share at just 10 percent. The headline set was almost entirely Hormuz: the proposed Iran-US deal on inbound traffic, the Iran-Oman route understanding, and crude slipping below 80 dollars.
